The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=3.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=6?$
question.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=6$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,6].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(6)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(1)=3,$ and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{1}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=1$ to $t=6.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{1}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t=1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(6)=3+1=4.
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=6$ is $x=4.$
